text: Two types of hormones, classified by the way they interact with target cells:
Water soluble hormones cannot cross the lipid membrane, and thus interact with cells by binding to external receptor
Fat soluble hormones are able to diffuse across the lipid membrane, and thus interact with cells by binding to receptor sites within the cytoplasm (e.g. sex hormones)

Consider the following situations and make predictions:
A patient complains of persistent fatigue, feeling cold and weight gain. Their doctors confirms via blood test that they have hypothyroidism. What would their
and TSH levels be on a blood test?

Low thyroxine, but high TSH. Patient is not at homeostasis, and since their thyroxine levels are low, there is a constant release of TSH trying to stimulate the thyroid gland to produce more thyroxine.
2. Let’s consider a different patient who had their thyroid gland removed due to cancer. What would you expect their TSH levels to be?
Their TSH levels would be high again. There is no thyroxine produced at all, but the hypothalamus/pituitary gland do not know that there is no thyroid
, so they continue to try to stimulate it anyways.
3. A third patient has a pituitary tumor that is leading to an overproduction of TSH.. How would this impact their levels thyroxine and TRH? What symptoms would you expect?
Thyroxine would increase, and therefore we would observe symptoms of hyperthyroidism. TRH levels would be below normal.
